why: Leave-one-year-out may train on records from later calendar years, so it is not a prospective hindcast. Preserve it as interpolation sensitivity, not the main scientific success gate.
primary_validation: Rolling origin: year t=2010...2017, fit only eligible patch-year triples whose t_train<t, hence all their outcomes (at t_train+1) are known by t; predict binary nonoccupancy in t+1 using only covariates observed at or before t.
support: Use exactly frozen 10,061 occupied consecutive patch-year triples, and only complete-case covariates or training-only imputation.
fixed_covariates: Same baseline and interaction as MELITAEA_19YEAR_FALLBACK_FIT_ADDENDUM_V01.json; no response-driven hyperparameter adjustments.
report: raw decline high/low count and risk within strict forward test only
forward year-by-year baseline and augmented log loss
forward overall logloss and Brier improvement
bootstrap by patch and year separately, 2000 draws
retain old leave-one-year-out results clearly labeled nonforward
primary_pass: forward gain >0, full patch bootstrap lower CI>0, full year bootstrap lower CI>0, and >=6 of 8 forward years show improvement
failure: If not passed, do not call host-loss buffering a novel predictive result; no post-hoc year/window/cutoff searches.
scope: observational next-year non-detection; no causal host removal, nonnative impacts or evolutionary history
